Answer: C
Reason: The CT images (Figures 4a and 4b) clearly show high-density, radiopaque material within the pulmonary arteries, which is characteristic of polymethylmethacrylate (bone cement). Combined with the history of recent vertebroplasty and a sudden drop in end-tidal CO2 (indicating acute pulmonary embolism), this confirms a diagnosis of cement pulmonary embolism.
